title: Hedging around results and events
summary: Why an overnight gap jumps past a stop, and the three answers: avoid, close before, or hedge, with what protection costs.

questions.q: Why can a stop-loss fail on results day?
options: Stops don't work on results day by rule
The price can open far beyond the stop with no trade in between
questions.why: A gap skips every price in between, so the stop fills at the open.

questions.q: Which is NOT one of the three ways to handle an event?
questions.why: Turning the stop off removes protection; the other three reduce the event risk.

questions.q: Why does protection cost more just before results?
options: Implied volatility is higher, so options are pricier
questions.why: Expected big moves raise IV, and with it every option's price.

questions.q: You sold a put for ₹7 and protection costs ₹6. The sensible choice is usually to:
questions.why: Paying ₹6 to protect ₹7 leaves almost nothing; closing is cleaner.

questions.q: Where does the builder show results before your expiry?
questions.why: The builder lists results and dividends before expiry as warnings.
